💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the big Diablo 4 Developer Revision has indeed delivered the goods.
  • You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.
  • Industry observers note that season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the big Diablo 4 Developer Revision has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Industry observers note that season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

Sources indicate that patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

When you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

According to recent reports, starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the newly introduced Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

It has been revealed that if you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a new event that rewards you for killing enemies quickly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

According to recent reports, the Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

Anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

According to recent reports, there are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

Sources indicate that the other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a latest item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Recent findings suggest that even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the upcoming season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

In a recent development, the trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the latest class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

It has been revealed that season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

Recent findings suggest that the more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

Sources indicate that fnatic has confirmed the departure of its longest-serving player, jungler Razork, who is set to join Team Heretics. With support Lospa also set to leave, the London club faces a near-total LEC roster rebuild for 2027.

Recent findings suggest that fnatic has made its first confirmed exit official as it rebuilds its LEC roster for 2027. Razork was the London club’s longest-serving player and its main playmaker. He leaves after five seasons in the jungle.

According to recent reports, the club marked the departure with a farewell video titled “Thank You, Iván”. In it, Fnatic recalls him arriving as a young player with huge ambition. He had entered the LEC with Misfits Gaming in 2020 before moving to Fnatic in 2022. The club later extended his contract to run through 2026.

Sources indicate that his next stop appears to be Team Heretics. Sheep Esports reported that the 26-year-old will play alongside midlaner Jackies and support Jun. Heretics had already tried to sign him a year earlier. On that occasion it agreed a buyout with Fnatic but could not agree terms with the player.

The rebuild runs deeper than the jungle. Every Fnatic team member except Lospa was due out of contract in 2026. The support was signed until the end of 2027.

That deal will not keep him at Fnatic either. Lospa has reportedly agreed verbally to join SK Gaming for 2027. No buyout is involved in moving his contract between the two clubs. With that move, the one contract running beyond 2026 also leaves the club.

In the jungle, Yike is set to replace Razork in a 2027 line-up of Soboro, Yike, Vladi, Doggo and Labrov, according to Sheep Esports sources.

The overhaul follows a difficult year. Fnatic finished eighth in LEC 2026 Versus. It then placed seventh in Spring, which ended on 10 May. Summer brought the same finishing position.

A loss to GIANTX on 30 August kept the team out of the Summer playoffs. That defeat left the club absent from Worlds for the first time since 2016.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that after a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go. Though, if you do, be prepared for bugs and crashes, as work on the mod is far from over with the release of this "true beta".

As shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts. In that regard, it seems more akin to GTA 4's online mode than GTA 5's, with classic improvised hijinks the main draw over being able to pull off gigs with a crew. Though, there do also look to be roleplaying servers which could scratch the itch of those more interested in pretending to be a merc than blowing up other people's rides.

Recent findings suggest that "After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord. "Anyone can jump in and play now — no invites or applications needed. Fair warning: this is a true beta. Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers. We welcome everyone: regular players, future server admins, and those who just love breaking game mechanics.".

"Right now, our absolute priority is stability and fixing crashes," they continued later in the post. "Latest features are planned, but we need to polish the foundation first. A huge thank you to everyone who has been with us since the early versions, helped with closed testing, and patiently waited. We've finally reached this milestone. Let's see how the project handles real player traffic!".

According to the modders, CyberMP's "client doesn't have a digital signature yet", which could cause antivirus software not to be a fan of it. They're also anticipating "problems with the anti‑cheat system", so it may be worth holding off on giving the mod a go if you're not keen on being trolled by someone with the sort of destructive power usually reserved for megacorps and AIs from beyond the blackwall in the Cyberpunkverse.

It has been revealed that for info on how to get CyberMP up and running, as well as create a custom server dedicated to the likes of roleplay or races, head over to its website. As you might expect, the mod requires a legit copy of Cyberpunk bought on either Steam, GOG, or the Epic store.

Industry News: Scientists discover a upcoming type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (981 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A newly identified form of depression may help explain why some people struggle to find relief from commonly prescribed antidepressants.
  • The discovery emerged from an analysis of clinical and genetic information from more than 10,000 Australians with depression.
  • Sources indicate that circadian depression is associated with the body's 24-hour internal clock, which helps regulate when we feel awake and when we feel sleepy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A newly identified form of depression may help explain why some people struggle to find relief from commonly prescribed antidepressants. Researchers at the University of Sydney have discovered a subtype called "circadian depression," which appears to be closely connected to the body's internal biological clock.

The discovery emerged from an analysis of clinical and genetic information from more than 10,000 Australians with depression. Nearly one-quarter of the participants in the study, which focused on people with severe, recurrent or persistent depression, revealed characteristics of this newly identified subtype.

Sources indicate that circadian depression is associated with the body's 24-hour internal clock, which helps regulate when we feel awake and when we feel sleepy. People with this form of depression tend to respond less favorably to common serotonin-based antidepressants. However, treatments that target the brain circuits involved in controlling circadian rhythms, including melatonin, melatonin-targeted antidepressants and light therapy, may offer more effective options.

Published in the British Journal of Psychiatry, the findings shed light on the genetic factors associated with this subtype and offer a possible explanation for why widely used medications such as SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) are less effective for some patients.

A Hidden Type of Depression Affecting Nearly One in Four Patients Studied.

To investigate the biological differences between forms of depression, researchers examined information collected through the nationwide Australian Genetics of Depression Study. Their analysis included clinical histories and genetic data from more than 10,000 people who had experienced depression.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers identified nearly 25 percent (2,604 participants) as having circadian depression. Several recognizable patterns distinguished these individuals from other people with depression.

Sources indicate that those with the circadian subtype were more likely to experience seasonal changes in their depression, sleep for longer periods when depressed, and wake up feeling exhausted despite spending more time in bed. They were also more likely to be night owls, meaning they naturally preferred staying awake late and waking later in the day.

It has been revealed that the differences extended beyond sleep patterns. Depression often began earlier in life for these individuals, and their symptoms tended to be more severe (such as mania and higher levels of suicidal thoughts). Genetic analysis also revealed an increased predisposition to inflammatory and cardiovascular health problems, along with major neurodevelopmental disorders, including ADHD.

It has been revealed that first author Dr. Emiliana Tonini from the University of Sydney's Brain and Mind Center said:.

"Our research has identified circadian depression as a new subtype, affecting around a quarter of people in our study into those with severe, recurrent or persistent depression.

"Depression is not a uniform illness, and understanding the characteristics of different subtypes means that we can give people earlier access to treatments that will be most effective for them.".

Why Common Antidepressants May Be Less Effective.

One of the most notable implications of the discovery involves how depression is treated.

Medications such as SSRIs and SNRIs (serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors) are generally among the first treatments offered to people diagnosed with depression. These drugs work by influencing chemical messengers in the brain that help regulate mood.

However, the researchers found that these medications tend to be less effective for people with circadian depression. Individuals with this subtype also experience more side effects, suggesting that conventional antidepressants may not be the best initial approach for everyone.

According to recent reports, because circadian depression is closely associated with the body's internal clock, therapies designed to influence that clock may be particularly useful. Light therapy, for example, uses controlled exposure to bright light to help regulate biological rhythms. Melatonin, a hormone involved in signaling when the body should prepare for sleep, and antidepressants that target melatonin pathways may also be relevant treatment options.

Recent findings suggest that co-senior author Dr. Jacob Crouse from the Brain and Mind Center explained:.

"Because circadian depression is linked to people's internal body clock, treatments targeting the circadian rhythm, such as light therapy and melatonin, may be much more relevant, and clinicians should reach for these much earlier in people with this presentation.

"For those who find that antidepressants are not working for them, it is important to speak to your clinician for advice about your individual circumstances.".

A Latest Approach Could Improve Depression Treatment in Young People.

Recognizing circadian depression earlier could be especially important for younger patients, who may otherwise spend valuable time trying medications that are less suited to their particular form of depression.

Professor Ian Hickie, Co-Director of the Brain and Mind Centre and a clinical psychiatrist, warned that failing to identify this subtype in young people can contribute to unsuccessful early treatments and unnecessary side effects.

According to recent reports, the findings highlight the importance of recognizing that depression is not a single, uniform condition. Different biological mechanisms may contribute to similar symptoms, meaning that treatments effective for one person may provide much less benefit to another.

By identifying patients whose depression is closely tied to circadian rhythms, clinicians may be able to offer more targeted treatments earlier rather than relying on the same initial medication approach for everyone.

"We really want young people to receive the most appropriate treatment early in their course of illness.

"Most young people will be offered SSRIs first up, but for at least a quarter there are better circadian-focused medical and behavioral options to help treat and manage their condition.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, while many of Grand Theft Auto 6’s craziest moments happen out of the blue while freeroaming, others are rewards for helping out strangers with their extended questlines. These questlines can be picked up in a variety of ways, rewarding players for scrolling Snapmatic or keeping an open eye around the world.

One such questline centers around the strawberry farmer Kyle McKittrick, a man who needs a hand or two ensuring that his special growth formula wins the local strawberry competition. As is GTA tradition, this simple premise spirals rapidly, giving a glimpse of Rockstar’s take on a Marvel legend, but only if you can find him.

According to recent reports, kyle’s questline can be started as early as Chapter 1, provided you spot his Snapmatic post while scrolling as Jason. Look for a post featuring a prop plane and open it to get the quest marker far to the north of the Keys. This is a major detour from any of the story content in Chapter 1, so don’t worry about waiting, Kyle isn’t going anywhere.

When you have time, drive up to his farm, and he’ll ask whichever protagonist you’re playing to pilot his prop plane and douse his strawberry fields with his own blend of growth hormones. This is a super chill mission, all you need to do is dump the chemicals above where Kyle is parked, dousing both him and his strawberries on each run. He’ll pay you for your help and ask you to keep in touch for any updates.

Sources indicate that after around 24 hours in-game, Kyle will call Jason and Lucia, asking them to pick up a supply of chemicals from a local biker gang. Once you arrive at the marked location, you’ll call him again for some extra context. He explains that the bikers will be expecting payment, but he doesn’t care how you get the chems either way.

According to recent reports, the goal is to leave the compound with the van filled with Kyle’s chemicals, all else is secondary. At first, the bikers will demand $5,000 for the van, but it can be easily bartered down to $3,000. Refusing their price will start a fight, and it can be difficult to get the van off the premises with a sea of angry bikers.

I’d recommend paying the bartered-down cost if you can afford it, allowing you to safely drive the van out and park it at Kyle’s to complete the quest.

Wait a bit longer for another message from Kyle, or keep an eye on his Snapmatic account for a video where he highlights off his insanely massive strawberries before running off camera. Return to Kyle’s farm one final time to find an armed outfit of government agents attempting to get him to come outside.

To sneak in, enter the chemical van parked nearby, where you can slip on a hazmat suit to blend into the crowd. Head behind the barn and two guards will escort you inside, revealing Kyle’s new, Hulkish form. He’ll throw open the doors of the barn, and the assembled agents will open fire.

According to recent reports, if you do nothing, Kyle will die, so take out the two guards still beside you in the barn and assist Kyle with clearing the rest. Once you do, he’ll fall to his knees, where you can comfort him and give him a hug for a huge boost in Professional Criminal Profile points.

It has been revealed that after you calm him down, Kyle will leap off, surely to assist against a future alien invasion of some kind. Thus ends one of Grand Theft Auto 6’s wildest questlines, shifting from farming assistance to superhero origin story at the drop of a hat.

  • The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

According to recent reports, since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Patch to actually see it in action.

It has been revealed that the Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

In a recent development, the Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside upcoming Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the massive day.

Latest Update: New gum disease treatment kills bad bacteria while sparing the good

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1158 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers in Japan have developed a promising upcoming treatment for gum disease that kills harmful bacteria while leaving beneficial microbes unharmed.
  • Developed by scientists at Nagoya University, the treatment combines antibodies obtained from egg yolks with near-infrared light.
  • Why Conventional Gum Disease Treatments Can Cause Problems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers in Japan have developed a promising upcoming treatment for gum disease that kills harmful bacteria while leaving beneficial microbes unharmed. Unlike conventional approaches that can eliminate both good and bad bacteria, the new therapy is designed to target specific microbes responsible for damaging gums and the bone that supports teeth.

Developed by scientists at Nagoya University, the treatment combines antibodies obtained from egg yolks with near-infrared light. Early experiments in human cell cultures and mice suggest that it could offer a more precise way to combat periodontitis, a serious form of gum disease that can eventually lead to tooth loss. The findings were published in the Journal of Translational Medicine.

Why Conventional Gum Disease Treatments Can Cause Problems.

Industry observers note that the human mouth contains a complex community of microorganisms, many of which play notable roles in maintaining oral health. Problems can arise when harmful bacteria multiply and disturb this delicate balance.

It has been revealed that one particularly troublesome species is Porphyromonas gingivalis (P. gingivalis), which scientists classify as a keystone pathogen. This means it can have an outsized influence on the surrounding microbial community, even when it is not especially abundant. By promoting inflammation and disrupting the normal balance of oral bacteria, it can contribute to the destruction of the bone that holds teeth in place.

Treating periodontitis often involves eliminating the bacteria responsible for the infection. However, some existing antimicrobial treatments do not distinguish between harmful organisms and microbes that help maintain a healthy mouth.

It has been revealed that "Current treatments for periodontitis, including antibiotics and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT), eliminate both pathogenic and beneficial oral bacteria," remarked Kazuhide Sato, one of the corresponding authors and a lecturer at Nagoya University. "These approaches often disrupt the entire oral microbial ecosystem and can also release lipopolysaccharide (LPS), an endotoxin that may exacerbate inflammation.".

Scientists Adapt Cancer Therapy to Target Gum Disease Bacteria.

Sources indicate that to overcome these limitations, the Nagoya University team turned to a technology originally designed to treat cancer. Known as near-infrared photoimmunotherapy, it uses antibodies linked to a light-sensitive dye to recognize specific targets. Once the compound attaches to its intended target, exposure to near-infrared light activates the dye and produces a damaging effect.

In a recent development, the researchers adapted this strategy to attack P. gingivalis without unnecessarily disturbing other oral bacteria. Their approach relies on IgY, a type of antibody collected from the egg yolks of hens that have been immunized against the pathogen.

Egg yolk antibodies offer a practical advantage because they can be produced in large quantities at relatively low cost. This could make them an attractive option for developing targeted treatments that are affordable and scalable.

In a recent development, the resulting technology, called near-infrared photo-antibacterial targeting therapy (NIR-PAT²), was developed by researchers at Nagoya University Graduate School of Medicine. The team included first author Hiroshi Maruyama, Professor Hideharu Hibi, and corresponding authors Sato and Kiyoshi Sakai.

To determine whether the treatment could destroy harmful bacteria while protecting healthy tissue, the researchers tested it in human cell cultures and mice. They also compared its effects with those of conventional antimicrobial therapies.

Light-Activated Antibodies Destroy Harmful Bacteria.

Laboratory experiments showed that the antibody and dye combination attached specifically to P. gingivalis. Other bacterial species and healthy human gum cells were left unaffected.

When the researchers illuminated the targeted bacteria with near-infrared light, the activated dye damaged their outer membranes, ultimately killing them.

Microscopic examination revealed an key difference between this technique and conventional antimicrobial light therapy. Bacteria exposed to the new treatment developed tiny openings in their membranes but largely maintained their overall shape. By contrast, conventional antimicrobial photodynamic therapy caused the bacteria to break apart completely.

It has been revealed that the distinction matters because destroying bacterial cells can release substances that contribute to inflammation. Preserving the overall structure of the targeted bacteria, even after killing them, could help limit this unwanted effect.

The researchers also examined how the treatments affected healthy human gum cells. Their targeted therapy caused no detectable harm to these cells, while conventional antimicrobial photodynamic therapy produced cellular damage and slowed healing.

New Treatment Reduces Bone Loss in Mice.

The team next investigated whether these laboratory findings would translate into meaningful improvements in gum disease.

In mice with periodontitis, the experimental therapy significantly reduced the loss of alveolar bone, the part of the jawbone that surrounds and supports teeth. Preventing this type of bone deterioration is especially notable because advanced periodontitis can loosen teeth and eventually cause them to fall out.

Sources indicate that analysis of the animals' saliva revealed another encouraging result. The treatment reduced P. gingivalis while preserving beneficial Streptococcus bacteria, helping maintain a healthier balance of microorganisms in the mouth.

Conventional antibiotics and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy, on the other hand, eliminated both harmful and beneficial bacteria in the experiments, causing broader disruption to the oral microbial community.

"Results demonstrated that, unlike antibiotics or standard light therapy, this approach selectively removes the primary pathogenic species while preserving the remainder of the oral bacterial community," Sato remarked.

Together, the findings suggest that targeting individual disease-causing bacteria could help control gum disease while avoiding some of the unintended consequences of broader antimicrobial treatments.

AI Could Help Develop More Precise Gum Disease Treatments.

In a recent development, although the early results are promising, the researchers recognize that periodontitis is a complex disease involving multiple bacterial species. Eliminating P. gingivalis alone may not be sufficient to treat every case.

Industry observers note that to address this challenge, the team aims to use artificial intelligence (AI) to examine publicly available information about oral bacteria. By identifying other key microorganisms and studying how different species interact, they hope to uncover additional targets for future therapies.

The researchers also see potential implications beyond oral health. Periodontitis has been linked to several other medical conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis and diabetes.

It has been revealed that understanding the relationships between oral bacteria and these conditions could eventually help scientists identify which patients are most likely to benefit from specific treatments. AI analysis may play a role in making those decisions and guiding the development of more personalized approaches to gum disease.

For now, the therapy remains experimental, with its effectiveness demonstrated in laboratory studies and mice rather than human clinical trials. However, the findings point toward a possible future in which treating gum disease means selectively removing harmful bacteria instead of disrupting the entire microbial community that helps keep the mouth healthy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shopify Rebellion Black opened the North America Qualifier Playoffs with a 2-0 win over Xora Esports. The non-partner organisation is now one win from the playoffs that decide a guaranteed São Paulo Kickoff place.

The best-of-three Group Stage meeting with Xora began at 00:10 UTC on Saturday 21 November, opening Shopify Rebellion Black’s VCT Americas Kickoff: North America 2027 campaign.

Sources indicate that the result counts for more because Shopify Rebellion is now outside Riot’s partnership system. The organisation was one of the Americas sides that stated it had not been chosen for the 2027-2028 partnership programme, Sheep Esports reported. Cloud9, ENVY, M80, FlyQuest and LYON were also on that list. Riot now has eight partner teams in each of its four regions.

The Swiss Stage runs from 20 to 22 November 2026. Every match is best of three. Two wins send a team through to the playoffs, and two losses knock it out. The eight teams left after the Swiss phase move into a double-elimination bracket played over six competition days, with the playoffs set for 1 to 6 December. The event is listed as an online, A-Tier Riot Games qualifier for 16 teams.

It has been revealed that shopify Rebellion Black’s next opponents are Oafs, who also won their opening match 2-0, against QoR. Both teams are therefore one win from the playoffs. Oafs already have a record against Xora. They knocked them out of the Qualifier 1 bracket on 8 November with a 2-1 win. Xora had still reached the Qualifier Playoffs by finishing joint third in the 512-team North America Qualifier 1.

Across 83 rated matches, Shopify Rebellion Black hold a 59-24 record. Before this event their most recent series was a 2-3 defeat to 2GAME Esports at the VCL Americas Last Chance Qualifier 2026. Earlier in that event they had beaten 2GAME Esports 2-1 and Contra 2-0.

It has been revealed that the organisation’s second line-up had a harder start. Shopify Rebellion Gold lost 0-2 to Maryville University. Several of the other organisations left out of the partnership programme won their first matches. Cloud9 beat counterfeit 2-0, Team Envy beat Yellow Dragon Gaming 2-0 and FlyQuest edged Masterclass 2-1. Elsewhere, Winthrop University beat SaD Esports 2-0 and YFP Gaming beat Wildcard 2-1.

Sources indicate that the prize for coming through the bracket is a place in São Paulo. Riot will stage the 2027 VCT Americas Kickoff in Brazil. Its eight Partner Teams get direct entry. Non-partner teams can win four places: one guaranteed slot each for North America, Brazil and Latin America, plus one for the Americas Last Chance Qualifier. For a non-partner side, a later run to Masters would be worth a fixed US$200,000 and a place at Champions US$400,000, Dot Esports reported. The regional Kickoff events are due to start on 14 January 2027 and run until 7 February 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Nobody was hurt" in a shooting last week near the California office of Clockwork Revolution developers InXile, both the studio and local police have confirmed. The incident, which took place on November 11th, is at the moment being investigated and police have reportedly taken a suspect into custody.

"Officers got there [on November 11th]," Tustin police sergeant Christopher Peterson stated in statement to Aftermath. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why.".

In a recent development, "We’re relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," a spokesperson for InXile stated in a separate statement. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate.".

InXile are set to release steampunk RPG Clockwork Revolution next year. The studio, developers of the likes of Wasteland 3 and The Bard's Tale IV, are one of the few Xbox-owned studios not to have been affected - at least as of writing - by Microsoft's ongoing mass layoffs this year.

Since being revealed in 2023, Clockwork Revolution's dripped with Bioshock-ish vibes and popped up semi-regularly at Xbox showcases. "Wield the power of an incredible device to travel back in time, changing the past and rewriting the future of the city you call home: the vibrant steampunk metropolis of Avalon," reads its Steam synopsis. "In this immersive RPG, you'll step into the shoes of Morgan Vanette, a fully customizable player-character and member of the Rotten Row Hooligans. Travel between past and present as you battle the ruthless Lady Ironwood, who has been manipulating time to keep the working class struggling while amassing immense wealth and power.".

Best wishes to the staff at InXile, here's hoping that going forwards they're able to get with making what's looking to be an intriguingly funky game without enduring any more concerning incidents like this one.

Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto has never shied away from, well, anything really. Political corruption, gang violence, culture clashes, both the underworld and sleazy heights are well within Rockstar’s sights, both in their main campaigns and plethora of side content.

With Grand Theft Auto 6’s small-scale start, it can be easy to forget that, with various side missions here to remind us. One such mission without a name, one I’ll just be calling the Near Fatal Sex Scandal, sees a woman begging for help on the side of the road. Want to learn more, and even how to start it yourself? Let’s get straight to it then.

According to recent reports, while driving down the US-70 post Chapter 2, you may hear a woman crying for help, clad in a bathrobe. If you stop to help her, she’ll explain that someone up by the house needs your help, and beg you to follow.

In a recent development, follow her, and she’ll escort you through a very fancy southern style manor, before approaching a bedroom. She asks for your complete confidentiality before opening the door, revealing her husband, a right-wing politician, unresponsive in a sex swing.

Interact with the body to help her get him down, where she’ll realize he’s already dead. Quick on her feet, she demands you help dispose of the body, pointing you to the river just down the hill as the perfect spot. Pick up the corpse as she rushes you out to continue.

As you carry the body down the hill, the politician himself will begin to stir, startling the player character, who drops him to the grass. Stunned and betrayed by his wife’s seeming attempt on his life, he’ll demand you back him up. Follow him back to the estate and allow him to interact with the bedroom door.

His wife, again not missing a beat, immediately pivots back into their roleplay, belittling him and yanking her “bad little globalist” back into the bedroom. For your trouble (and trauma), you’re tossed a cool $10,000, an absolute game changer if found early enough in Chapter 2.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is back to its seams with all kinds of small encounters like this, perfect for a quick joke and a pocket full of cash as you pursue Jason and Lucia’s perfect life.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next massive game has officially launched.
  • The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.
  • Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next massive game has officially launched. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

According to recent reports, in Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially launched, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

It has been revealed that numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game at the moment sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, an IBM quantum computer has completed an extraordinarily complex computational task in just 15 minutes, while leading methods for simulating the calculation on conventional computers would require prohibitively long runtimes. Perhaps even more significantly, researchers were able to establish statistical confidence in the accuracy of the quantum computer's results, addressing one of the biggest obstacles in the field.

The achievement, led by IBM and researchers from the University of Chicago, satisfies the fundamental criteria for quantum advantage. This milestone occurs when a quantum computer performs a computational task beyond the practical capabilities of leading classical computing methods while producing results that can be trusted.

In their fresh paper, "Sampling hard circuits with verifiably high fidelity," the researchers demonstrated that both objectives could be achieved simultaneously using a novel design for encoded quantum circuits. The experiment represents one of the largest demonstrations of logical quantum computing to date. The researchers have also made their circuits and experimental results publicly available through the Quantum Advantage Tracker.

Solving Quantum Computing's Verification Problem.

Unlike conventional computers, which process information using bits that represent either zero or one, quantum computers rely on quantum bits, or qubits. These can exist in combinations of both states and interact through a phenomenon known as quantum entanglement. These properties allow quantum computers to approach certain computational problems in fundamentally different ways.

For years, scientists have tested the capabilities of quantum computers using a benchmark called random circuit sampling (RCS). This technique involves running a series of randomly selected quantum operations and generating samples from a complex probability distribution. As the circuits grow larger and more complicated, reproducing their output with a classical computer becomes increasingly difficult.

It has been revealed that however, this approach creates a fundamental dilemma. If a computation is too difficult for a classical computer to reproduce, how can researchers establish that the quantum computer performed it correctly?

As computational complexity increases, independently verifying the results becomes progressively more difficult and eventually impractical without making strong assumptions about how accurately the quantum hardware operates.

To overcome this problem, the IBM and University of Chicago team developed a more structured alternative to random circuit sampling. The researchers mathematically demonstrated that their approach preserves the same computational hardness criteria as conventional RCS while introducing a structure that allows errors to be detected during the computation.

"Verification remains one of the biggest challenges in firmly establishing experimental quantum advantage," said Bill Fefferman, Associate Professor at the University of Chicago. "This experiment develops techniques to better characterize the fidelity of hard quantum states under noise, increasing confidence that the quantum computer is solving a computationally hard problem.".

Soumik Ghosh, PhD student in Fefferman's group at the University of Chicago, added, "Beyond strengthening experimental validation, advances in verification have the potential to unlock practical applications for the next generation of quantum computers.".

70 Logical Qubits and Tenfold Lower Error Rates.

One of the greatest challenges in building powerful quantum computers is their extraordinary sensitivity to errors. Quantum information can be disrupted by environmental disturbances, imperfections in hardware, and inaccuracies in the operations used to manipulate qubits. As computations become longer and more complex, these errors can accumulate and undermine the reliability of the results.

Sources indicate that quantum error correction addresses this weakness by encoding quantum information across multiple physical qubits to create more reliable units known as logical qubits. This approach allows certain errors to be identified and, depending on the technique, corrected or accounted for without destroying the underlying quantum information.

In one of the largest known demonstrations of quantum error correction, the researchers performed computations using 70 protected logical qubits. The experiment involved 2,415 logical two-qubit operations and 468 logical "T gates.".

Quantum gates are the fundamental operations that manipulate quantum information, much like logic gates in conventional computers. Two-qubit gates allow qubits to interact, while T gates enable additional types of quantum operations needed for universal quantum computing. Together, these gate counts illustrate the considerable complexity of the experiment.

By encoding the quantum circuits, the researchers achieved effective logical error rates 10 times lower than the underlying physical error rates. This substantial reduction allowed the quantum computer to maintain remarkably high fidelity, a measure of how closely the actual quantum state matches the intended one, despite performing thousands of complex operations.

It has been revealed that "We are now firmly in the quantum advantage era," remarked Jay Gambetta, Director of IBM Research and IBM Fellow. "We have demonstrated a quantum computation beyond the practical reach of classical computers that establishes, with statistical confidence, a lower bound on how faithfully it was executed. This milestone gives scientists, developers, and businesses a fresh foundation for trusting quantum computers as they scale to problems far beyond what we can achieve classically.".

The researchers found that many leading classical simulation techniques would require impractically long periods to reproduce the computation. IBM's quantum computer, by comparison, accomplished the task in approximately 15 minutes.

Although the experiment was designed to demonstrate quantum advantage rather than solve an immediate real-world problem, it addresses two essential requirements for making large-scale quantum computing practical: controlling errors and establishing confidence in computational results.

By demonstrating both capabilities in a computation beyond the practical reach of leading classical methods, the researchers have taken a significant step toward a future in which quantum computers could reliably tackle scientific and industrial problems that are at the moment out of reach.

No Org No Problem won the opening and deciding maps against Stallions Esports to reach the MENA Qualifier Playoffs grand final. One more series win against Mix My Miks would send them to VCT EMEA Kickoff 2027 in Berlin alongside partner teams including Fnatic.

Recent findings suggest that against Stallions Esports, the semi-final went the full distance. No Org No Problem took the opening map in 48 minutes. Stallions Esports levelled on the second, winning a 54-minute contest. No Org No Problem then closed out the decider in 43 minutes.

Stallions Esports won Middle East Qualifier 2 from 16 to 18 November, ahead of Mayhem. Mix My Miks won North Africa Qualifier 1, a single-elimination event from 9 to 11 November, ahead of BAAM Esports. Each of those qualifiers had 64 teams.

Industry observers note that mix My Miks booked their final place by beating Gamax Esports in the second semi-final. That match also went to three maps. The four-team playoffs are being played online in a single-elimination bracket. The semi-finals were best of three.

In a recent development, alongside the MENA winner, Europe sends two qualifiers to Berlin and Türkiye sends one. The partner teams already in the field are BBL Esports, Fnatic, FUT Esports, Gentle Mates, Karmine Corp, Team Heretics, Team Liquid and Team Vitality. Fnatic were confirmed in October 2026 as staying on as a VCT EMEA partner for 2027.

It has been revealed that the tournament will be played in person at the Riot Games Arena in Berlin in early 2027. For the MENA winner, the trip carries direct financial value. Riot’s support for non-partner teams starts at Kickoff, and the sums rise for teams that progress further through the season.

Recent findings suggest that non-partner teams that qualify for Masters receive US$200,000, and those reaching Champions receive US$400,000, Dot Esports reported. Europe’s route to Kickoff runs in parallel. The Europe Kickoff Qualifier Playoffs begin with a Swiss stage from 25 to 29 November, followed by playoffs from 3 to 5 December.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3.
  • Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB.
  • It has been revealed that to begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related issues.

Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

It has been revealed that to begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja noted it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

The more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

According to recent reports, the amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

It has been revealed that patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

In the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

It has been revealed that speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

There’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

10 Fighting Game Remakes That Improved Everything From The Original Games

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1476 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I still look back fondly on those afternoons at my grandmother's house, sitting in front of the TV with my cousins and firing up my PlayStation 1 for hours of fighting games like Tekken 3—a series I'm still playing with Tekken 8—and Mortal Kombat Trilogy, one of the best games with non-stop violence that ever existed.
  • Recent findings suggest that still, the genre hasn't always been perfect.
  • Recent findings suggest that fortunately, some of those games got a second chance through exceptional remakes that fixed every flaw from the originals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I still look back fondly on those afternoons at my grandmother's house, sitting in front of the TV with my cousins and firing up my PlayStation 1 for hours of fighting games like Tekken 3—a series I'm still playing with Tekken 8—and Mortal Kombat Trilogy, one of the best games with non-stop violence that ever existed.

Recent findings suggest that still, the genre hasn't always been perfect. Plenty of classics rolled out with serious balance problems, rough performance, or questionable mechanics that could easily sour the experience.

Recent findings suggest that fortunately, some of those games got a second chance through exceptional remakes that fixed every flaw from the originals. Here are 10 fighting games that completely reinvented themselves with fresh mechanics, features and definitive balancing.

As a longtime JoJo's Bizarre Adventure fan, I was excited when All-Star Battle got its Western PS3 release in 2014 (following its 2013 Japanese debut). That hype faded fast once I felt its 30 fps frame rate, slower combat pacing, and a Campaign mode weighed down by stamina timers and microtransactions.

Sources indicate that in 2022, Bandai Namco released JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: All-Star Battle R on PS4, PS5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S, Switch, and PC. While the Switch version runs at 30 fps, the PlayStation, Xbox, and PC editions target 60 fps, immediately making combat feel snappier to me. It also added an Assist system for extending combos and expanded the roster across the series.

Best of all, it dropped the original Campaign's stamina timers and energy purchases—though the game still features paid DLC characters and costumes, and solo players lost the original Story and Campaign modes in favor of the panel-based All-Star Battle mode. For me, the faster gameplay made that trade-off worth it.

According to recent reports, not every necessary remake is modern. While the 1993 arcade Virtua Fighter was a landmark title, its 1994 Sega Saturn port was rough, with flat, untextured polygonal models and distracting polygon flickering.

It has been revealed that released in 1995 for arcades and the Saturn, Virtua Fighter Remix tackled those early-port challenges head-on. Side by side on Saturn, the jump is clear: Remix introduced texture-mapped character models with far sharper facial and outfit detail. It wasn't a flawless fix—some polygon glitches remained, the lighting shifted, and load times increased—but for Saturn owners at the time, it was still a major visual upgrade that stood up much better alongside early Tekken.

After falling in love with Bloody Roar 2, playing Bloody Roar 3 on PS2 (following its 2000 arcade debut) left me wanting more. Its animal-transformation premise was still a blast, but to my eyes, the early-PS2 visuals looked rough, with jagged edges and coarse textures.

It has been revealed that in 2002, Bloody Roar: Primal Fury rolled out on Nintendo GameCube (followed by Bloody Roar Extreme on Xbox in 2003) as an enhanced remake of Bloody Roar 3. Compared to the PS2 release, the GameCube version offered cleaner character models, upgraded lighting, animated endings for the cast, and newcomers like Cronos and Ganesha. Personally, it became my go-to way to play the game, making every match feel far more polished and satisfying.

I've loved Street Fighter for years, but jumping into specific Western arcade revisions of 1994's Super Street Fighter II Turbo—notably the World 940223 and USA 940323 builds—was a rude awakening. Both are notorious for a difficulty bug that makes the CPU unusually fierce regardless of the machine's setting, on top of lopsided matchups involving Old Sagat, Vega, and a tournament-banned Akuma.

Sources indicate that when Super Street Fighter II Turbo HD Remix hit PS3 and Xbox 360 in 2008, I was immediately won over. Udon Entertainment redrew the sprites and stages in HD, and the game added a rebalanced mode to rein in dominant fighters while still letting purists play under the original rules. Paired with built-in GGPO rollback netcode, it became a much friendlier way to enjoy a classic.

Sources indicate that the PS2 introduced me to countless classics, including Dead or Alive 2: Hardcore (an updated PS2 edition of the 1999 arcade and 2000 Dreamcast fighter). I loved its fast pace and multi-tiered stages, though its early-PS2 visuals aged quickly and its counter-heavy combat could feel unforgiving.

Dead or Alive Ultimate arrived on the original Xbox in 2004 with a ground-up remake of DOA2 built on an upgraded DOA3 engine. Compared to the PS2 version, the leap in lighting, textures, and stage detail was night and day. While reversals remained a defining—and sometimes divisive—part of the formula, Ultimate felt like the definitive package, bringing together fighters like Tengu and Bayman alongside DOA3's Hitomi and over 20 interactive stages.

At launch, it also stood out for its Xbox Live lobbies and spectator mode—a huge draw at the time, even though Microsoft officially shut down original Xbox Live servers in April 2010.

In a recent development, SNK's catalog deserves a spot in any fighting game discussion, including The King of Fighters 2002. This fantastic Neo Geo game had strong core gameplay, but its presentation felt more stripped-back to me than SNK's earlier classics, with a soundtrack that didn't hit as hard and several NESTS-saga favorites missing from the roster.

In a recent development, I also wasn't a fan of a meta dominated by Billy Kane, Athena, and Choi. That's why the 2009 remake, The King of Fighters 2002: Unlimited Match (originally on PS2, later coming to Xbox Live Arcade in 2010 and PC in 2015), felt like such a triumph.

Expanding the roster to 66 playable characters in its console and Xbox Live Arcade editions, it overhauled the stages (using 3D polygonal backgrounds on PS2 and 2D replacements on PC), added a fresh soundtrack, refined MAX Mode cancels, and introduced new moves across the cast—turning it into one of my favorite 2D fighters SNK has ever made.

The original Karateka rolled out in 1984 for the Apple II before receiving ports for Atari 8-bit systems, the NES/Famicom, and the Commodore 64. Its flaws stood out rapidly, though: the controls were slow and stiff, there were no checkpoints—meaning a single lost fight sent you right back to the beginning—and the combat system was bare-bones.

In 2012, however, a remake arrived on Xbox 360 before making its way to PC, PS3, and iOS. This newly introduced version rebuilt the visuals from the ground up in cel-shaded 3D powered by Unreal Engine 3, and introduced a one-on-one combat system built around visual and audio cues for countering attacks. What really won me over was how it replaced the single-life structure with three consecutive suitors, each with different speeds and their own unique endings.

In a recent development, at launch, the original Fatal Fury: King of Fighters—released in 1991 for Neo Geo—drew plenty of criticism for offering only three playable characters: Andy Bogard, Terry Bogard, and Joe Higashi. On top of that, its gameplay lacked depth, relying on a simple three-button control scheme.

In a recent development, in 1999, Fatal Fury: Wild Ambition hit the Hyper Neo Geo 64 and PlayStation 1, expanding the roster to 12 fighters in arcades and 14 on PS1. It also introduced newly introduced defensive and meter-management mechanics, including the Heat Meter, Heat Blow, and Overdrive Power. It's worth noting, however, that Sony's console version took several noticeable graphical downgrades compared to the arcade release.

Industry observers note that this title might not be as widely known as others on this list, but it had a strong following in Japan back in the day. Asuka 120% Burning Fest. originally rolled out in 1994 for the FM Towns, though several issues held the experience back—including a limited roster, a lack of defensive tools, and the fact that it was locked to a niche Japanese home computer.

Sources indicate that several years later, in 1999, Asuka 120% Final: Burning Fest. Final arrived on PS1. While it remained a Japan-only release, this version featured a completely rebuilt combat engine with a much faster pace and noticeably smoother sprite animations. It also expanded the character roster—adding secret fighters into the mix—and introduced deeper offensive and defensive mechanics, such as air recovery.

The original Eternal Champions introduced on the Sega Genesis/Mega Drive in 1993 in North America, followed by Europe and Japan in 1994. Like many entries on this list, though, it suffered from frustrating complications—including punishing AI, clunky, unintuitive controls, and a small roster, among other flaws.

It wasn't until 1995 that its remake, Eternal Champions: Challenge from the Dark Side, which can be considered one of the best fighting games stuck on older systems, arrived on the Sega CD as an expanded overhaul of the original. It expanded the starting roster from nine to 13 fighters—alongside a large lineup of unlockables—introduced upcoming FMV finishers called Cinekills, and improved the difficulty curve compared to the original game.

Sources indicate that as his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm. Capcom has provided the following character summary:.

It has been revealed that cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

Recent findings suggest that in addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

It has been revealed that mega Man: Dual Override launches in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:.

As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

Industry observers note that the standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the firm's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be unveiled tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

Industry observers note that this batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

According to recent reports, last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

The Sims 4 will soon get a new enhancement to resolve a number of issues, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it prepares to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

Industry observers note that you can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most important is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

In a recent development, going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

Speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis said this will work with fresh and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

Pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in new saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

It has been revealed that you may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a newly introduced lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Industry observers note that lower down the list of urgent fixes is an upgrade that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently confirmed that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.

The BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Kurtaj, now aged 21, was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial. He'll be sentenced at a later date.

Kurtaj carried out the 2022 Rockstar hack while on bail for other hacking offences and being housed at a Travelodge hotel under police protection, the latter on account of rival hackers threatening to attack him over stolen Bitcoin stashes. The Rockstar hack was reportedly done using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into the hotel room's TV, plus a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

It has been revealed that 90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by that hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the company contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

Earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by "Cyberleek" posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent organization Take-Two quickly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

Hopefully with the game's console release later this week, those will be the only two GTA 6 leaks which have to be added to the annals of gaming history. As much as marketing can leave a bad taste in the mouth, especially when it barely shows anything of the actual product being advertised, neither of the GTA 6 leaks served much of a purpose beyond forcing people to waste some time and energy talking about the perpetrators.

There were many discussions before finalising the roster, and a lot of it came down to the gameplay and systems in place, along with The Pokémon Firm's own requests. Here's what Harada had to say about this (via EventHubs):.

Industry observers note that harada: "We had thorough discussions before finalizing the roster. There were Pokémon that the development team wanted to include from a gameplay and systems perspective, and of course, The Pokémon Company also had its own requests for which Pokémon they wanted to see in the game.".

After the release of Pokken Tournament DX for Switch, the final roster included the following Pokémon (this included some Switch-exclusive and DLC Pokémon).

In a recent development, as you can see, the final roster is an interesting mix. Harada, who is now the CEO and game director of SNK's VS Studio, added how he was just personally happy at the time to see the lineup include Pikachu and Gengar.

In Vice City, you can never come too prepared for a fight. Between the nightlife and our protagonist's penchant for causing chaos, it’s a good idea to stay strapped in case of an emergency.

The only issue is that in those opening hours, you’re pretty limited in what you can get because money is fairly tight. If you’re looking to buy guns, you don’t want to waste your money on something that feels suboptimal.

According to recent reports, this list includes a bunch of good weapons you can get in the first couple of chapters of the game. It feels a little crazy that the early game can stretch so far in hours, but GTA 6 really is a humongous game.

It has been revealed that the Duval Signature ES9 is basically a more powerful version of Jason’s starting weapon, and it’s a great weapon to keep on you at all times. While it is a sidearm, it can still be helpful in all kinds of situations.

The key part of this one is that it has incredibly high handling, meaning you’ll pretty much always hit what you aim for. In the early hours of the game, that can be the difference between life and death.

At a certain point in the game, you’ll be able to grab Donnie’s sidearm and keep it for yourself. This small but mighty weapon is great for people looking to take people out promptly at a shorter range.

Sources indicate that you won’t be able to take on a whole army with it, but it fits nicely into an extra slot for when things start to get a little dicey. Donnie is a crazy guy, so it makes sense his gun is just a little crazy too.

According to recent reports, most people will probably feel like a sniper is relatively useless, especially when the cops start to roll up on you. For the most part, that’s true, but with this weapon you can easily take out some people without getting spotted.

In a recent development, with high range, accuracy, and decent damage, you can put down just about anything you come across with relative ease. Just be sure you’re far enough away to not have to worry about when people start looking.

In a recent development, this weapon is an alternative assault rifle you can buy called a battle rifle, and it comes in handy when going up against big crowds of enemies. Not only does it pack a good punch, but you can stay in relative safety while using it.

The only real downside to this one is that using it a little too much might see you moving in a negative way with your Criminal Profile. That’s probably something you’re going to want to avoid if you’re hoping to stick to a happy ending.

Sources indicate that this lovely little piece does a great job at putting just about anything down, but you’ll still need to be choosy about how you fire. It does have great handling, but you could still find yourself in real danger if you get surrounded swiftly.

Aside from that, it’s a great weapon for car fights since it can pack such a good punch. If you’ve got the aim to use it, this bad boy can take on most any challenge, except maybe some truly unhinged NPCs.

A fancy found weapon, the Scrapper VF5C, is a great weapon to get, especially before you start getting into the really crazy parts of the game. Silenced and ready for action, this gun will be a great tool for taking on even the toughest jobs.

In a recent development, it does lack some stopping power, but with such high handling, it’s relatively easy to use, and that’s a very good thing. As long as you’re smart with it, there’s virtually nothing this weapon can’t handle.

One of the best early-game weapons that you can grab basically right at the start is the Wortham W-14. It’s a little tough to use, but once you have the hang of it, you can put down anyone who crosses your path.

It’s a fantastic weapon, especially if you’re looking to keep your Criminal Profile on the lighter side. One shot is really all you need with this one, and with such high accuracy, it hardly ever misses the mark.

Sources indicate that probably the best early-game longarm weapon you can get, this found weapon will make swiss cheese out of anyone you want. It’s got high damage and good handling, but you’ll be on your own for aiming and distance.

This gun is phenomenal for almost any scenario, but especially in situations where you’re running into a lot of people. Whether it’s the foot or the face, you’ll only ever need to shoot once at someone to take them out of the fight.

In a recent development, of course, it wouldn’t be a Rockstar game without including some choice references, and what a reference it is. With this lovely piece as a nod to Red Dead Redemption, you’ll find yourself operating like a real cowboy on the streets of Vice City.

The gun is only available as part of the Ultimate Edition, which is a little problematic, but despite that, it isn’t the only powerful early-game sidearm. It does pack quite the punch and lets you pick off enemies from a distance.

The best early-game weapon of all is a found weapon you can get from pretty much the opening hours of the game. This small silenced pistol is great for committing all kinds of nefarious acts without ever having to worry about getting caught.

It has been revealed that while its damage is low, it’ll never give away your position and can quickly put holes in people with ease. It works best if you’re looking to avoid complete shootouts, but really you could pretty much use it whenever in this insanely good simulation game.
