Sources indicate that the line-up of ExpMoe, calamity, vanitas, yearn and dynamic was one of eight teams Riot Games invited directly to the North America Qualifier Playoffs. Cloud9, ENVY and two Shopify Rebellion line-ups were also on that list.

Sources indicate that before facing Maryville, QoR edged Shopify Rebellion Gold 2-1 in round two. In the Swiss stage, two wins sent a team through and two losses knocked it out. QoR sit 99th in the Elo power rankings, with a rating of 1590 and a 37-34 record across 71 rated matches.

According to recent reports, maryville came through the second open qualifier, held from 12 to 15 November, which drew 512 teams. They finished in the top two of that bracket. They then opened this event by sweeping Shopify Rebellion Gold.

Industry observers note that A 0-2 loss to Cloud9 followed, and defeat by QoR left them with two losses. In the other round-three matches, Oafs beat SaD Esports, counterfeit beat FlyQuest and Wildcard beat Winthrop, each without dropping a map. The Elo table places Maryville 161st, with a rating of 1521 and a 6-7 record in 13 rated matches.

According to recent reports, the playoffs are an eight-team double-elimination bracket. The winner takes North America’s direct place at the 2027 VCT Americas Kickoff in São Paulo. The runner-up goes to the Americas Last Chance Qualifier, also in São Paulo, on 17 and 18 December. That event is the last route into Kickoff. Eight partner teams are invited to Kickoff, and four places go to non-partner teams.

Industry observers note that riot runs the North America qualifiers with Red Bull. They also serve as the North America qualifiers for Red Bull Home Ground. The Los Angeles event runs from 10 to 13 December. Ten teams will play for a total prize pool of $100,000 USD. Eight are invited from around the world, and two earn their places through regional qualifiers. Riot will also reveal the 2027 Kickoff draws live on stage there.

Sources indicate that fnatic are EMEA’s invited team. The organisation is rebuilding its roster after parting with several players, including long-serving captain Jake ‘Boaster’ Howlett, Red Bull stated.

Breaking: PS5 Exclusive Destruction AllStars Shuts Down On November 25

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, playStation embarked on a live service push a few years ago, and there’s a trail of bodies lying in its wake, most of which never even saw the light of day.
  • Industry observers note that in May of 2026, PlayStation delisted Destruction AllStars along with the game’s virtual currency.
  • At the time of writing this, that date is tomorrow, which means if you have continued to play Destruction AllStars offline, your fun is about to forcibly come to an end.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, playStation embarked on a live service push a few years ago, and there’s a trail of bodies lying in its wake, most of which never even saw the light of day. Destruction AllStars did make it out alive, but only just. The PS5 exclusive hasn’t been available to buy for a while, and from November 25, it will no longer be playable at all, barring one unsupported feature.

Industry observers note that in May of 2026, PlayStation delisted Destruction AllStars along with the game’s virtual currency. It gave those who still play the game a little more time to keep playing offline, with the promise that it will end service on November 25, 2026.

At the time of writing this, that date is tomorrow, which means if you have continued to play Destruction AllStars offline, your fun is about to forcibly come to an end. Server support will officially be shut down at 3 pm UTC on November 25. That’s 10 am EST, so technically you will still be able to play for a little while tomorrow too.

You might actually still be able to play after that time has passed, as PlayStation’s shutdown statement clarifies that the game’s single-player arcade challenges might still be available. Emphasis on the “might”, as with support for the game being pulled entirely, if something were to immediately break, which seems likely, there will be no one on the other end to fix it.

It has been revealed that if you have any of that aforementioned virtual currency left, now is the time to spend it. Once Destruction AllStars is shut down, that money will simply disappear. If you do still have any left over, you have effectively already lost it since anything you buy today will be gone by tomorrow.

Destruction AllStars managed to avoid the live service grim reaper for five years, although that is giving the game a lot of credit it definitely does not deserve. When PlayStation unveiled it would be shutting down the game and ended multiplayer service effective immediately, it had basically been broken for two years.

The same statement that confirmed the game’s shutdown noted that multiplayer services would remain offline indefinitely due to “ongoing technical issues”. It remains unclear, and may stay that way forever, whether PlayStation was actively trying to fix the problems for all that time and couldn’t figure it out, or it simply didn’t care due to lack of player interest and eventually let everyone know that it wasn’t even trying to fix things behind the scenes.

According to recent reports, destruction AllStars will be a relatively small footnote when gaming historians inevitably write about PlayStation’s infamously poor live service push. Concord’s cancelation and Naughty Dog being forced to waste time and resources on a game that would never be released, The Last of Us Online, will be the focus. It’s a footnote all the same, though, and had it been a more notable release, its immediate failure might have forced PlayStation to rethink this whole live service thing before it led to layoffs and studio closures.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales.
  • All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they declared a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".
  • The lawyers in question are from Robbins LLP, who specialise in "shareholder, whistleblower, antitrust, & consumer litigation".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales. The class action lawsuit in question claims that Intel's distribution and manufacturing partners have had to deal with "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", and that the gains from Intel's investments in AI datacenters aren't enough to make up for slowing sales of PCs to regular Josephines who just want fancy boxes they can play Deadlock on.

All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they declared a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".

The lawyers in question are from Robbins LLP, who specialise in "shareholder, whistleblower, antitrust, & consumer litigation". In a press release, they say they've filed suit on behalf of anybody who bought Intel stock from July 23rd to October 29th this year.

The suit claims that Intel neglected to tell investors that falling PC and component sales were having a "materially greater negative impact" on their third financial quarter 2026 Client Computing and Physical AI Groupresults than Intel had previously stated – to the tune of "hundreds of millions of dollars" in revenue shrinkage, compared to the previous quarter, with the situation still expected to "worsen".

They also accuse the organization of keeping schtum about the aforesaid "massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", together with the fact that "any positive impacts to Intel’s business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset by the negative effects on the Company’s business and financial results resulting from the PC market slowdown and the excess inventory buildup described above.".

Finally, they say Intel bosses have failed to disclose that they're struggling to procure an adequate supply of substrates – that is, materials used to create the base layer of chips, circuit boards and similar components. As such, the lawyers claim, Intel couldn't "ramp up production to meet data center CPU demand even if the Firm chose to divert production resources because of a slowdown in PC-related sales.".

Recent findings suggest that once the Godzilla of personal computing, Intel haven't been having a brilliant few years. Back in 2024, they recorded a multi-billion dollar quarterly loss, pushing then-CEO Pat Gelsinger to resign. As regards sales of gaming PCs, they've fallen behind AMD, though they've reportedly taken some ground back recently as regards desktop CPUs. As regards graphics cards, they have long been dwarfed by Nvidia.

Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

Industry observers note that with the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

It has been revealed that that same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

In a recent development, it’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

Sources indicate that and, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

In a recent development, crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

GodLike Esports beat Trigger Point Esports 2-0 in the upper bracket of the VCT Pacific Kickoff South Asia qualifier. Only two South Asian sides will reach the Last Chance Qualifier, where a single place at Kickoff in Bangkok is on offer.

Industry observers note that godLike Esports opened their VCT Pacific Kickoff: South Asia – Qualifier 2027 playoff campaign with a 2-0 win over Trigger Point Esports on Monday 23 November 2026. GodLike took both maps of the best-of-three upper bracket quarter-final. Trigger Point Esports now drop into the lower bracket of the double-elimination format.

The playoffs are being held online by Riot Games and JioBLAST. Series in the bracket are played as best-of-three or best-of-five.

GodLike arrived in form. They reached the playoffs with an unbeaten 4-0 record in the open qualifier, VLR.gg reported. They shared joint first to fourth place in that event, which ran from 17 to 20 November. Trigger Point finished in the group placed fifth to eighth.

GodLike fielded Karam1L, Paradox and RvK from India, alongside sayoo from Indonesia and azyshaha from the Philippines. Sabyasachi ‘Antidote’ Bose is listed as head coach, with Samar as substitute. Trigger Point’s listed players are SangraM, WEELJACK and RaJ.

South Asian teams cannot qualify directly for Kickoff. The top two from the playoffs join the Oceania playoff winner and the Southeast Asia playoff runner-up in a four-team Last Chance Qualifier. Only its winner goes through to Kickoff in Bangkok, according to Dot Esports.

In a recent development, the stakes are high. Twelve teams will play at Kickoff, and the top three will qualify for Masters 1. The route stays narrow later in the season too. South Asia has no direct place at the Cups, with Cup 1 in Manila and Cup 2 in Tokyo. It sends two teams to an eight-team Pacific LCQ, and the winner takes the last Cup place.

Sources indicate that the qualifier also has a fresh organiser. Riot picked JioBLAST to run the South Asia qualifiers instead of NODWIN Gaming, the previous organiser. Riot has not remarked why it made the change.

The UK interest lies with SIGN Esports. They beat Zexar Esports 2-0 in another upper bracket quarter-final. Russel ‘Russ’ Mendes joined SIGN Esports on 16 November 2026. He is the only player from the UK in the eight-team playoff field.

Russ was born in 1998 and is of Indian descent. He won the VALORANT Challengers 2025 South Asia Grand Final with Velocity Gaming on 13 July 2025, when they beat S8UL 3-1.

GodLike Esports and SIGN Esports both remain in the upper bracket, one defeat away from the lower bracket. Trigger Point Esports and Zexar Esports must win from the lower bracket to stay in contention for a top-two finish. The playoffs run until 29 November 2026.

Industry observers note that it seems that Naughty Dog can’t get enough of Tom Holland, after he starred in their blockbuster live-action Uncharted adaptation. Appearing as Nathan Drake, Holland was a hit with fans and casuals and the film raked in over $400 million at the global box office.

Now, the studio appears to have tapped Holland again to star in the next installment in their cinematic universe, with a upcoming report placing the English actor as signed on for the much-rumored project.

In a recent development, A latest report through Production Weekly indicates that Holland is attached to a Jak & Daxter adaptation, a film which he has expressed a personal desire to appear in in the past. His name appears under the cast section, with the film being directed by Ruben Fleischer, who helmed Naughty Dog’s previous Uncharted adaptation.

It has been revealed that the Production Weekly glitch is from June 2025 but was recently unearthed by fans, and appears to be reputable, as it connects with a previous report from the same time that A Minecraft Movie writers Neil Widener and Gavin James had signed on to write the screenplay. Production Weekly is a long-running trade newsletter that tracks upcoming film and television productions, including details on projects in development, pre-production, and active filming.

[Holland’s] name appears under the cast section, with the film being directed by Ruben Fleischer, who helmed Naughty Dog’s previous Uncharted adaptation.

The project was set for a tentative 2026 shooting date, being filmed in London by Sony Pictures Entertainment. A synopsis of the movie reads: “After Daxter falls into a Dark Eco silo at the forbidden Misty Island, he is transformed from a human into an ottsel, a fictional hybrid of an otter and weasel. In a quest to return Daxter to human form, he and Jak set out to find the Dark Eco sage Gol Acheron. However, the duo find Acheron corrupted by Dark Eco, choosing to use the elusive Light Eco to defeat him and save the world at the cost of Daxter remaining in his ottsel form.”.

Sources indicate that holland himself has previously expressed that he’d love to play Jak in any planned adaptation, saying in 2022: "I would like to make a Jak and Daxter movie, and I would play Jak... But I would make it A24, so it was really weird and dark. Yeah, I would do a really weird live-action version of Jak and Daxter." No details about the film except the synopsis are available, or whether it'll be as dark as Holland hopes.

A live-action Jak & Daxter adaptation would be the first time the franchise has made it to the silver screen, and would certainly breathe new life into Naughty Dog’s dormant IP, which hasn’t seen any new games since 2009’s Jak and Daxter: The Lost Frontier on PlayStation Portable. Despite the huge gap between releases, the franchise is still a cult classic and has a legion of dedicated fans—with Naughty Dog surely feeling another box office success starring Holland would be a great way to attract a new generation of players to their iconic duo.

Despite the huge gap between releases, the franchise is still a cult classic and has a legion of dedicated fans.

In a recent development, some players believe that the film may come alongside a major remake of Jak & Daxter’s original outing, which debuted in 2001 on PlayStation 2. It would certainly follow the ongoing trend of studios remaking their classic titles for modern audiences, and would indicate a back to basics move for Naughty Dog after its major successes with Uncharted and The Last of Us franchises.

Whether Naughty Dog is willing to invest that much time and money in reviving a series still remains unknown, but it would certainly push the 3D platformer back into the public eye and hopefully mirror successes of other PlayStation classics that made the jump to modern consoles, like Spyro The Dragon and Ratchet and Clank.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield Studios has revealed that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week.
  • According to recent reports, though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous.
  • According to recent reports, for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield Studios has revealed that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

According to recent reports, though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

According to recent reports, for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Once downloaded, you’ll find a latest Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

In a recent development, once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the newly introduced Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

Recent findings suggest that all-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Recent findings suggest that casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Industry observers note that casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

According to recent reports, the most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

This is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a massive upcoming revision - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, this week sees the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, the open-world crime 'em up that's been in development for at least eight years and has been waited on by fans for even longer. Naturally, over on PC we're still waiting for a port to be revealed, let alone a release date to circle in our calendars. But, as happens whenever a latest GTA is on the horizon, I think about Mafia: City of Lost Heaven.

Released less than a year after Grand Theft Auto 3, Mafia is perhaps a more prescient example of Rockstar's future than their own.

Set in Lost Heaven, a shoe-in for 1930s Chicago, Illinois, you play through Tommy Angelo's rise from a taxi driver, who has a chance run in with the Salieri crime family, to one of the gang's main enforcers in their fight against their rivals, the Morellos.

In a recent development, the influences on developers Illusion Softworks are obviously cinematic, with whole sequences ripped from The Godfather films and Goodfellas (and I'd argue there's a sprinkling of Once Upon A Time In America for good measure). A habit they share with Rockstar, who also pull liberally from crime films that share the settings of their games. But Illusion Softworks are also clearly interested in capturing the history of the Prohibition era, too. The story begins in the aftermath of the 1929 Wall Street Crash and the depression that followed, running through until the late 30s, and you see that time pass in the city around you. Buildings that are under construction at the start of the game are completed by its end, a used car lot in Chinatown sits empty for most of the game until business picks up with the economy, but most enjoyable of all is that the cars driving the streets change. At first the roads are filled with Ford Model-T-inspired vehicles that basically look like horse carriages with engines, but by the end of the game they've all become much sleeker creatures that have left their early carriage influences behind.

It has been revealed that the city Illusion Softworks built also has a dedication to verisimilitude that we see Rockstar adopting in their later games. As you drive Lost Heaven's streets, you must pay attention to speed limits and red lights, as speeding and running traffic lights will both earn you a fine if a policeman spots you. For fans of public transport, there are streetcars and overhead trams you can ride to navigate the city, too. Two other touches I love: when you reload your gun, you dump the whole clip instead of returning the unfired bullets to a magic ammo reservoir, and vehicles can run out of fuel if you drive them too far.

Much had been made of all the simulations running under the surface of Grand Theft Auto 6, such as fully realised cloud formation, a smell reaction system, and… fuel tanks that can run empty. No doubt they're significantly more impressive than what's on show in Mafia, and this isn't about putting the two games against each other (even if one of them was likely made for less than the other studio spent on coffee runs across its eight-year development). Nor is it about saying history recognised the wrong game: Grand Theft Auto 3 was a huge step forward in open-world gaming and Mafia was recognised and celebrated in its time. It's about something else.

Back in 2002, Illusion Softworks offered a different kind of open-world crime game. One that was more mature despite having a lower age rating. Grand Theft Auto was undoubtedly more influential, sparking imitators that mostly opted to follow its tone and sensibilities – Saints Row began in a similar place to GTA 3 and as the series continued leaned further into the silliness and parody, for instance. But while for many years Mafia stood as a sign to an open world path that could have been taken, the longer Grand Theft Auto series has gone on, the more Rockstar have found their way toward the example set by Illusion Softworks. The games are still aiming for bombastic comedy at times, but they're also interested in the likes of newly-arrived-in-America Niko Belic, or Michael de Santa, a retired criminal haunted by his past. They're much richer protagonists than Claude, the silent character you play in GTA 3.

The Mafia series has continued, marked by ideas that remain as interesting as what was on show in the original. In Mafia 3, you play Lincoln Clay, a black soldier returned from the war in Vietnam and brought into the family. Set in a take on Fresh Orleans, Louisiana, during the civil rights movement, you face overt racism. Linger too long in white, wealthy neighbourhoods and the residents will call on the police to move you along. And the Definitive Edition remake of the first game, released in 2020, is a rare example of a game that both captures the spirit of the original and justifies its existence by expanding and bettering the story. Though I don't think any of its sequels have been as innovative, nor as forward thinking, as the first game.

I don't want to come across as Rockstar-bashing. The studio have continued to push the open-world genre forward with every release and I want to see what other developers lift from GTA 6 for their own games. But I'm even more pleased that as the studio's aged, their work has grown closer to Illusion Softworks'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major update. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Recent findings suggest that unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

As everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the significant focus of this revision, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot new arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this enhancement. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

According to recent reports, if he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

It has been revealed that returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Sources indicate that version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a newly introduced activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

Tech Report: Rockstar Is Reportedly Eager To Turn Red Dead Redemption Into A Movie

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (476 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has become commonplace for an adaptation of a latest video game to be declared weeks after that game has been released if the hype is high enough.
  • That's according to a upcoming report from The Ankler covering Rockstar's continued reluctance to even consider GTA: The Movie.
  • Sources indicate that that report claims Rockstar is not only open to turning Red Dead Redemption into a movie or show, but it is actively shopping its second most successful series.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has become commonplace for an adaptation of a latest video game to be declared weeks after that game has been released if the hype is high enough. That will not be the case for GTA 6. Despite its success, Rockstar remains staunch in the belief that its hit series never needs to be turned into a video game or a TV show. Red Dead Redemption, on the other hand, is a different story.

That's according to a upcoming report from The Ankler covering Rockstar's continued reluctance to even consider GTA: The Movie. Even though the report was published last week, the day before the launch of GTA 6, it has only just started to land on people's radars as they stumble out of their homes after spending a collective 80,000 years in Leonida.

Sources indicate that that report claims Rockstar is not only open to turning Red Dead Redemption into a movie or show, but it is actively shopping its second most successful series. According to an agent who works with video game writers, the asking price for Red Dead's adaptation rights is $100 million. That's less than half of what Amazon paid for the Lord of the Rings rights, so it could make Rings of Power, and an absolute steal when compared to the reported $800 million price tag Xbox slapped on the adaptation rights for its biggest IPs, which were apparently showcased as a package deal.

While it might not be GTA, it feels like it might be worth that nine-figure price tag if a studio is confident it can do the Red Dead name justice. I'm sure Rockstar would be heavily involved should a project enter production, and likely wouldn't let anything that makes the series seem "less than" ever see the light of day. It certainly wouldn't be a repeat of what happened to Halo's two-season run on Paramount.

The willingness to have someone adapt Red Dead Redemption while remaining steadfast in its reluctance to see GTA become a movie one day, despite video game adaptations being all the rage, makes a lot of sense. Although still open, the Red Dead games are more linear and story-driven than any of the GTA titles. GTA 6 might be the most story-driven game in the series so far, and even that has so many ways players can go, with millions of us all experiencing the game in wildly different ways.

Sources indicate that the Red Dead games have specific stories to tell, and there are talented people out there who can help adapt those stories for a different medium. Although Amazon is the studio I'd have the most faith in to handle a video game IP the right way, following its stellar work with Fallout, Red Dead Redemption feels like it would be much more at home on HBO.

The tentacles of my trade empire snake up towards France in the west, down towards Africa in the south, and off into Hungary in the east. Yet, I still can’t reach out and grasp the throne that sits right in front of me. I’m Marco Sanudo, and the throne of the serene republic of Venice eludes me.

I’ve shed blood in its name, the blood of someone else named Marco no less. I’ve managed to avoid punishment for that crime, despite the fact it earned me a fiefdom to rule while I’ve tried to up my patrician score enough to be the lucky party the next time a ruling Doge dies in office (or runs out their 10 year term). Sadly, Doge Leonardo, the mysterious masked lord who’s had an iron grip on power since the first couple of old blokes to hold the position in this playthrough popped their clogs, is proving incredibly tough to oust.

In a recent development, it should, in theory, help that he’s my best mate, thanks to a well-timed feast. It certainly did in being granted a pardon for offing that other Marco, but not even that and a plague which infected nearly everyone in the realm aside from me have paved the way to Dogedom. In the meantime, I’ve striven to gain wealth and influence. I’ve worked up to having four trade routes running at once, with goods like wine, iron, and textiles flowing from market to market across southern Europe and bringing a steady supply of coin back to my Venetian estate. I’ve built trade posts at the extremities of my routes, giving me the option of starting from further afield and reaching latest lands if the cash flow dries up closer to home.

This is where Crusader Kings 3’s Silk and Silver expansion has blended a bit with the game’s traditional feudal moneymaking to supercharge my coffers. The land holding I killed a dude for, the Proveditorate of Zara, means I’ve also had tax money from modern day Croatia to add to both my trade profits and the income my domicile generates on its own. I am, as the medieval kids say, minted.

Industry observers note that getting to the point of serious pocket clinkage is, as you might imagine given Silk and Silver’s focus on filling the game’s world with travelling merchant companies and wheeler-dealing republican patrician families, the beating heart of the expansion. A near-constant stream of notifications about prices of different goods I’m trying to hawk in different locations encourage me to regularly prune and re-work my routes so that max profits are being earned and no carrying capacity’s being wasted. The bubbling up of wars and plagues impacts prices in affected cities, making it a never-ending battle if you’re desperate to optimise everything within an inch of its life. I’ve found that degree of micromanagement unnecessary if the goal is just to keep a decent profit margin ticking over. Just remember to replace the trader assigned to a route if they die, recall them every few years so they don’t stress themselves to death, and check in every so often to re-evaluate whether you’re running goods that are suitably in demand.

In a recent development, if you stick at it for a decent amount of time, with a certain type of good - alcohol or jewellery, for example - your expertise in dealing in them increases, making it easier to sell for better prices. Trade routes left running between the same markets also gain boons from being in place for a long time, offering a counterpoint to rejigging them every five seconds to wring out a few more coins. Most of my routes have run along a path that includes stops at four markets, with the occasional location boasting a monopoly I’ve bargained for with the local ruler, so I don’t have to worry about competition at every stop.

Industry observers note that when you’re playing as a merchant who isn’t locked into the ruling inner circle of a republic, making your routes as lengthy as possible is one of the three moneymaking areas your firm can specialise in. That first one’s caravaneering, and is the one I leant into in a non-Marco Sanudo playthrough. Beyond that, you can become an expert loan shark, lending cash to rulers or paying their ransoms in order to recoup interest and collect hooks you can use for favours. Manufacturing expensive artifacts that can be sold individually to collectors for a profit is the third option. The latter two I’ve only dabbled in a little bit as of writing, having earned enough gold mostly from caravanneering to buy the land containing the city with my home market and be anointed a Sheikh. So, beginning as a landless merchant is a nice alternative to Crusader Kings 3’s long-established wandering adventurer starting point, with both allowing you to work your way up from lowly serf to landed lordly dynasty in your location of choice.

Sources indicate that if you’re after a more specific historical scenario, Silk and Silver has Guelphs and Ghibellines. This is where we find Marco Sanudo, as well as the other patrician family head I’ve played as thus far, Speronella Dalesmanni. The setup is that the Pope and the Holy Roman Emperor have had a bit of a tiff, essentially rooted in who should have certain powers, with different cities and powerful families in northern Italy taking either the Guelph (Pope-likers) or Ghibelline (Holy Roman Empire-enjoyers) side depending on what suits their goals or principles. I’ll be honest, aside from being another way to easily earn friends or enemies in the ruthless crucible of merchant republican politics, where votes and reputation-bolstering aid from other nobles are key, the situation’s not had a hugely obvious bearing on my playthroughs thus far.

I think the closest it’s come is during my Dalesmanni run, if largely due to the existence of the By God Alone expansion allowing a new branch of Catholicism, dubbed Italian Christianity, to be created. The initial conversion push from the bishop responsible led a number of my fellow northern Italian nobles away from the Roman Rite headed by his Popeliness, making the Guelph/Ghibelline split more clearly defined.

In the early hours of both my Sanudo and Dalesmanni playthroughs, I’ve been far more focused on simply trying to push the respective patrician families up the hill from posh toffs with naught but a vote and a manor to elected rulers of their great cities, with land holdings to match. Speronella’s situation in Padua is made incredibly tough by the fact she’s a woman in a world where every succession rule is designed to put blokes first, so I’ve had more success with Marco and his quest to become the Doge of Venice.

It has been revealed that as the head of a patrician family, one of select few elite clans who steer the oligarchical republic, I was faced with earning Marco enough respect among his fellow family heads that they’d consider voting him to the top of the succession list, thus securing his power whenever the current Doge got the boot. Pulling that off, while also not kowtowing to the requests and schemes of those same peers, isn’t easy. A large cocktail of factors go into determining whether another noble likes you enough to vote in support of your succession. There’s your patrician rating, which is upped by doing things which specifically show you to be good at this Italian noble house lark, such as establishing trade monopolies for the republic, gaining the Pope’s favour, or having close relatives who also hold key positions in the republic. However, how close a friendship you have with the target and how their character traits align with you also play a huge rule.

Thus it was that, at one point, Marco was best mates with the current Doge and had a decent patrician rating, but had only amassed 68 of the 72 points needed for said Doge to vote for him because the Doge was generous, and therefore didn’t care for Marco’s ambitiousness. That same Doge either liked or respected Marco enough to grant him a council position and the status of regent, but he would not back Marco to replace him permanently for love nor money. This is the same man who liked Marco so much that when I pulled off that not-so-sneaky murder on another noble house head in order to inherit the keys to the Proveditorate of Zara, the Doge was instantly willing to pardon me and prevent Marco suffering any punishment for the crime.

Not even a couple of serious plagues hitting Venice, which at one point had all three people ahead of Marco in the queue suffering from smallpox, could get him on that throne. Eventually, it took a bit of lucky timing when his Doge mate died of old age - a few years after beating smallpox - to finally install Marco as Doge. Given that delayed promotion, as of writing I’ve not yet had enough time in the massive chair to give a proper verdict on how it differs from regular feudal rulerdom in the long run.

What I can do instead is tell you a bit about the fun of council votes. The same pool of voters who in a republic like Venice, get a say in who succeeds the ruler, also vote on the passage of laws and decrees. One proposal you can put forward is a vote to change who exactly is allowed a seat in this voting pool. It defaults to just being heads of patrician families, but can be extended to include all vassals, or tightened up so only the Doge’s councillors or the ruler themselves have a say, that being the way despotism lies. As you can imagine, passing a change to who can vote can drastically change the state of play, either tightening up the number of folks who might oppose or support you, or bringing new folks into play in a fashion that dilutes individual power, but gives you more pieces on the board to mind or manipulate to your advantage.

Sources indicate that I’ve found it suitably tough to orchestrate successful votes to change laws and customs which medieval Italian noble families, expectedly, have firmly entrenched stances on. Getting rid of checks and balances, such as the requirement to vote on banishments or wars - so the Doge can rule as a despot - has proven one such challenge, as has changing laws governing men being prioritised over women. I tried to pass equal succession as a substitute for men being put first while playing as Speronella, but met an insurmountable wall of resistance due to the region’s culture and faith. So, all I could do was try to put my young male heir in the best position possible to make the sorts of gains I couldn’t.

Much easier to weasel into place, either through some canny swaying or the offering of hooks, are laws giving state backing or other priority to trading in certain types of goods. Alcohol, for instance, which certainly hasn’t hurt the profits of Marco’s two wine trade routes.

Thus, cash continues to flow through the tentacles of my trade empire in sizable globs. As he’s now Doge, I’ve got Marco using the ample funds of Venice’s treasury to build a new piazza and have him focused on making the city’s already-strong trade league even more formidable, by attracting new members from the few other northern Italian blocs.

While I’m fairly sure there are folks who’ll find Silk and Silver's constant barrage of trade route notifications annoying, or that their power-grabbing skills and sheer multitude of money-making means combine to make playthroughs less challenging than they could be, so far I've found it another enjoyably sonorous string to Crusader Kings 3’s bow. Above all else, playing as a merchant gives more reason to invest in stewardship skills beyond just maximising your tax yields, while the republican politics of the DLC's main region fleshes out rewarding intrigue-focused builds. Diplomacy and martial skills are less key, but still have their place at times.

If you’re an absolute stickler for historical accuracy, you may well find other things to gripe about, but aside from the Guelph and Ghibelline conflict fading into the background, I’ve found plenty to like in my quest to become top Doge.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Avengers: Doomsday is packed with heroes and villains from the past quarter-century of Marvel movies. But there's one all-powerful figure who is quite clearly being held back – and it's got fans wondering what (if anything) he will have to do in the upcoming battle against Doctor Doom.

According to recent reports, so, how do you solve a problem like Bob? The character, first introduced in Thunderbolts, is right now lying dormant and chilling at New Avengerz HQ after being twisted into Sentry, a Superman-like figure who can send people to The Void with but a mere thought. Can you really leave that on the table if you're going up against Doom?

Well, it's a discussion that has spilled over to Reddit, with audiences debating the ramifications of unleashing Bob onto the world.

"Sentry is obviously gonna be there as an absolute last resort since the Avengers probably don’t wanna risk the Void coming back until they have no other choice," one stated.

Another added, "Doom is a master manipulator. Giving him access to the Sentry/Void is like a death invitation.".

Others joke that Bob will simply be Bob for the entirety of Avengers: Doomsday, kicking his feet and doing the dishes while the rest of the team brings the fight to Doom. There's a suggestion, though, that any major deaths – including to Florence Pugh's Yelena – would turn Bob into the unstoppable Sentry once more, with no allies to help calm him down this time.

Personally, I think Bob is being held back just to continue the age-old question of 'Who would win in a fight?' Pitting Sentry against Doom too soon not only risks answering it, but risks making Bob's power level seem diminished when he could be saved instead of Avengers: Secret Wars.

Discover what happens next – and if Bob puts on the Sentry suit once more – in Avengers: Doomsday, out in the UK on December 16 and in the US on December 18.

For more, check out how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

Can GTA 6 make $2 billion in its opening weekend? One industry analyst has run the numbers, and seems to think so

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Let's review what we already know: there is a conservative estimate of 10 million pre-orders for Rockstar's latest game floating around - something buoyed by comments from Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick - and, even by the company's lofty expectations, we know the game is tracking "well above expectations" when it comes to pre-orders.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that we all know the story of GTA 5 making more than $1 billion in the first three days it was on sale, right? At the time, Take-Two believed this to be the fastest any entertainment property had achieved the impressive milestone - music and films included. It made history, and with ease. And it looks like GTA 6 is going to do even better.

At least, that's according to one analyst, Joost van Dreunen, a senior data analyst and great writer/numbers diviner who wrote some predictions in his respected SuperJoost PlayList newsletter. "My prediction: Take-Two announces opening-weekend sales above $2 billion by Monday, 23rd November," he wrote. And you know what? I reckon he's onto something.

Let's review what we already know: there is a conservative estimate of 10 million pre-orders for Rockstar's latest game floating around - something buoyed by comments from Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick - and, even by the company's lofty expectations, we know the game is tracking "well above expectations" when it comes to pre-orders.

It has been revealed that we also know a lot of people are shelling out for the slightly more pricey Ultimate Edition (£90). So many people are opting for the more expensive version, in fact, that Take-Two revised its financial forecast up to $3.5bn for the next financial quarter, thanks to "recurrent consumer spending" (something Zelnick clarified in an investor's call is explicitly linked to the Ultimate Edition). 10 million pre-orders, at roughly $100 per copy - that's $1 billion right off the bat.

In a recent development, "That’s two days faster than its predecessor," van Dreunen said, "and largely before anyone has even played the game." That other $1bn will come over the weekend. And then, per the analyst, the game will sell roughly another 28 million copies over the course of the first year it's on sale. "My forecast puts first-year sales at 38 million copies, only modestly ahead of GTA 5’s 35 million. The real difference may be how much revenue each player generates over the years that follow.".

But it's what follows in the newsletter that intrigues me most. "At the high end, [GTA 6] may just lift the entire industry with it," wrote van Dreunen. "In the face of AI slop and shitty mobile games that exist only to extract revenue, it will offer a reprieve. At a time when the industry is increasingly focused on making games cheaper and monetising players more aggressively, Rockstar is about to demonstrate the enduring appeal of spending a fortune to make something people actually want to play.".

So, even if you're dubious about the game and Rockstar's motivations for selling as many copies as possible, the launch of GTA 6 could be something that gives the industry a much-needed jolt of life, in the face of rampant layoffs and shrinking talent pools.

It's not all sunshine and rainbows ahead for Rockstar, though: amongst the frenzy of launch activity, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week, as the game goes on sale.

#86286. 10 Video Game Rivals I Was Never Actually Mad At

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

10 Video Game Rivals I Was Never Actually Mad At

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2415 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that truth be told, I have a bit of a thing for villains who aren't entirely wrong.
  • I will say that most of these are still very much ultimately in the wrong.
  • Note: There are spoilers for every game on this list, including some very significant ones.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that truth be told, I have a bit of a thing for villains who aren't entirely wrong. Give me an antagonist with a tragic backstory and a motive I can halfway get behind, and I will spend the entire final boss fight feeling a little bit bad about winning it. Some of the games on this list are old, which shows you how profoundly they impacted me at the time I played them.

I will say that most of these are still very much ultimately in the wrong. It’s usually their methods I have issues with, ranging from questionable to horrific. I'm not going to pretend otherwise. Nonetheless, I can’t bring myself to be angry at them, because they are somewhat justified in their actions, so let's take a look at ten video game rivals I was never actually mad at.

Note: There are spoilers for every game on this list, including some very significant ones.

Sources indicate that N's whole philosophy is quite uncomfortable when you really think about it: he wants every Pokémon set free, because he believes they are suffering in the care of their trainers. And I'm not being funny, but he kind of has a point. We have spent 30 years catching animals, keeping them in tiny balls and making them fight each other for badges. The entire anime’s premise is that Pikachu didn’t like being stuck in a Poké Ball!

N is so very intriguing, right from the first encounter. Black and White had already given you two rivals in Cheren and Bianca before you even leave your hometown, and yet here is a third one, with his own battle theme and a design that looks nothing like anyone else's in a Pokémon game. He can also hear what Pokémon are saying, and when he tells you that yours genuinely like you, you believe him.

Sources indicate that he reveals himself as the king of Team Plasma on the Ferris wheel in Nimbasa City, and later on, a legendary dragon chooses him without him ever throwing a single Poké Ball. You still beat him, though.

Recent findings suggest that it then turns out that Ghetsis found him abandoned in the woods as a child, raised him alongside Pokémon that had been hurt by humans and turned him into a puppet king, all so Ghetsis could be the only person in Unova with Pokémon. The poor boy never stood a chance. As someone who will never play a Pokémon game without her starter, I'd like to think I'm one of the good ones, but I do understand his concerns.

Recent findings suggest that kirby: Nightmare in Dream Land is the rare case where the hero causes all the trouble. King Dedede steals the Star Rod from the Fountain of Dreams, breaks it into seven pieces and hands them out to his friends, and suddenly, nobody in Dream Land can dream anymore. Considering this is the same king who once stole all of Dream Land's food, Kirby assumes the worst, and quite frankly, I can't blame him.

Recent findings suggest that the problem is that Kirby doesn't even let him explain. When the two of them meet at the fountain, Kirby refuses to listen to a single word and marches off to collect every piece. As far as we know, Dedede simply stays at the fountain the entire time, keeping an eye on things.

Industry observers note that then Kirby comes back, beats him and puts the Star Rod back in place, whilst Dedede hangs on to his feet and begs him not to. Out comes Nightmare, who Dedede had been keeping sealed away the whole time. Instead of saying "I told you so", he inhales Kirby and spits him into the sky to go and fix it, which is a lot more grace than I would have managed.

Sources indicate that lilith's backstory is a lot more relatable than you'd expect from the daughter of Mephisto. She was created as little more than an extension of her father, grew tired of the Eternal Conflict between Heaven and Hell, and ran off with the angel Inarius to create Sanctuary: a hidden world where renegade angels and demons could live in peace. They had a son, the others had children too, and those children became the Nephalem.

Now, the Nephalem turned out to be far more powerful than their parents, and that made the renegades nervous. Some of them argued that the children would draw the attention of Heaven and Hell and should be destroyed, and Lilith did not take that well: she hunted the renegades down and slaughtered angels and demons alike. A number of Nephalem died along the way, too, and I can’t lie: she kind of loses me here a little.

Subsequently, Inarius couldn't bring himself to kill her, so he banished her to the Void and used the Worldstone to weaken the Nephalem, which meant they eventually developed into what became mankind. I will note that her plans for her children weren't exactly selfless, either, since she always saw them as her own army. Still, the man she created them with was ready to wipe them out, and I can see how that might put someone in a bad mood for a few thousand years.

Industry observers note that maruki is the kind of man I'd trust with my problems instantly, which is exactly what makes him so difficult to fight. He joins Shujin Academy as the upcoming school counsellor after the Kamoshida scandal, he is incredibly easy to talk to, and he genuinely wants to help. He's also a researcher in cognitive psience, which is never a good sign in Persona 5.

Sources indicate that his story starts long before he meets the Phantom Thieves. When his girlfriend Rumi fell into a catatonic state after her parents were killed in a break-in, Maruki awakened a Persona that could rewrite cognition and used it to save her. It worked, but she forgot the trauma and him along with it, and he stepped out of her life so he wouldn't bring any of it back.

From there, his dream grew into a world without grief or suffering, where everyone gets the life they always wanted. The catch is that nobody gets asked: he convinced Sumire that she was her late sister Kasumi, and he'd happily do the same to everyone else. That takes away free will and the chance to grow through hardship, and he crossed that line long before we ever got involved. He isn't after money or power, though, and he truly believes he's helping, which is why his Palace was the one I least wanted to break into.

Sure, Sin is evil and the big bad, and thus the villain, but technically, we’re talking about every summoner who ever set out to destroy it. For hundreds of years, summoners travelled across Spira with a guardian or two, learned to call the aeons at every temple along the way and eventually made their way to Zanarkand for the Final Summoning. Once there, they would sacrifice a guardian to finally defeat Sin.

Sources indicate that the problem is what happens afterwards. That guardian becomes the Final Aeon, and once Sin is destroyed, Yu Yevon possesses it and turns it into the next Sin. The Calm that everyone celebrates is really just the newly introduced Sin being created and slowly gaining its power, and so the whole cycle starts over again.

Industry observers note that so why did they keep doing this for hundreds of years? Well, nobody knew until it was far too late. The sacrifice of the summoner and a guardian was common knowledge, but the fact that the guardian would become one with Sin was not, and summoners only learned the truth once they met Yunalesca in Zanarkand. By that point, you've gathered your aeons, travelled across the entire world and are about to go toe-to-toe with the biggest bad there is. I can't really blame a single one of them for going through with it.

Sources indicate that fou-Lu does not make a great first impression. Within minutes of waking up, he has two soldiers killed for bragging that the Fou Empire could crush dragons, and he looks rather pleased with himself about it. To be fair to him, he has just woken up from a centuries-long nap, and nobody is at their best first thing in the morning.

He is the God Emperor, the other half of Ryu and the founder of the Fou Empire, who went to sleep with a promise that he would take back the throne once he awoke. The current Emperor would rather he didn't. General Yohm hunts him across the country, sets forests on fire and throws monster after monster at him until Fou-Lu crashes into the woods, barely alive.

Recent findings suggest that he wakes up in a little farming village, where a kind woman named Mami takes care of him, and for a while, it's genuinely sweet. Then imperial troops show up, Mami helps him escape, and the Empire fires at him. Before he blacks out, he realises that Mami's life was used to power the weapon. Wanting to wipe out humanity might still be a bit much, but quite frankly, I'd be grumpy too.

Loewe's backstory is incredibly bleak: he grew up in Hamel, a small Erebonian village near the Liberl border, and he was in love with Joshua's older sister, Karin. When the village was massacred to start a war, he lost his family and Karin, and he was right there when it happened. That alone would be enough to send anyone down a dark path.

Industry observers note that what really gets me, though, is what happened afterwards: once the war was over, the massacre was quietly covered up, and the official story was that a landslide had destroyed the road to the village. Loewe had no way of seeking justice and nobody to even acknowledge what happened, so he and Joshua made Karin's grave themselves.

So he joined Ouroboros, became its Enforcer No. II, the Sword Emperor, and set out to make the world face the injustices it would rather sweep under the rug. He is cold and terrifyingly strong whenever he shows up, but he still looks out for Joshua for Karin's sake. Without spoiling too much, finding out who was really behind Hamel only makes it worse.

In a recent development, I have played Tales of Symphonia more times than I can count, and Mithos gets more tragic with every single playthrough. Long before the game begins, he and his sister Martel were half-elves, hated by humans and elves alike, and driven out of their home because of it. Even so, they went on to end the Ancient Kharlan War together with Kratos and Yuan, and became heroes.

Industry observers note that then Martel was killed, and her dying wish for a world without discrimination turned into something rather sinister in his hands: the Age of Lifeless Beings, where everyone would be the same emotionless being, so that there would be nothing left to discriminate against. Over 4,000 years, that idea only gets worse. By the end, he is mostly fixated on bringing his sister back.

According to recent reports, the game clearly wants you to see him as the villain, but it also makes you understand him, and that is what makes him so well written. Raine and Genis have to hide that they're half-elves to protect her teaching job and his education, and even they can't fully dismiss his points. Tales of Symphonia is quite heavy-handed about discrimination, I will say, but it was pretty profound.

In a recent development, psaro's motivation is almost sweet, as far as wanting to wipe out humanity goes: he is in love with Rose, an elf who cries ruby tears. Naturally, greedy humans want those tears, not knowing that they break very easily, so Psaro builds her a little tower far away from all of them. Rose, meanwhile, keeps asking him to make peace with humans, which he refuses to do.

He isn't innocent, mind you. Egged on by his advisor Aamon, and after hearing that a human hero is prophesied to defeat him, he starts hunting down young humans, which is how the Hero's village gets destroyed at the start of Chapter 5. When Rose is then killed by humans, he loses it completely and transforms himself into Psaro the Manslayer.

In a recent development, the remakes added a sixth chapter, and that is why he made this list. You find a World Tree flower that can bring someone back from the dead, use it on Rose, and her tears turn Psaro back to normal. It also turns out that Aamon arranged her death to take over monsterkind himself, so Psaro joins your party to deal with him. He even got his own game in 2023, Dragon Quest Monsters: The Dark Prince, which feels like a well-earned redemption arc.

Industry observers note that saturos and Menardi were right, and boy, does that annoy me. For the entire first Golden Sun, they are the villains: they raid Mt. Aleph, steal the Elemental Stars and set off to light the four Elemental Lighthouses, which would release Alchemy back into the world. Alchemy was sealed away because it could destroy everything in the wrong hands, so naturally, you chase them across the continent and stop them.

Sources indicate that then The Lost Age hands you Felix, who has been travelling with them all along, and the whole story flips. Without Alchemy, the world of Weyard is slowly dying, and its edges are crumbling into the void. Their hometown of Prox sits right next to the Mars Lighthouse at the far north of the world, and it is drifting closer to that edge by the day. Menardi's younger sister Karst and her partner Agatio carry on where the first two left off, because their entire village depends on it.

Instead of explaining any of that, they went for sneaky and threatening, and they even kept Felix's family locked up in Prox to make sure he'd cooperate. I do understand why, though: nobody was going to believe two strangers claiming that the world was falling apart, especially when hardly anyone could ever travel far enough to see it. A little more communication would have saved everyone a lot of trouble.

Mailbox: Ocarina Intruders, Pikmin Day, Too Many Humans - Nintendo Life Letters

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1572 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nintendolife

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's just us here today - everyone else is busy in Hyrule or Leonida right now.
  • In fact, it's been like that for most of the month, it seems, as the Nintendo Life Mailbox is looking pretty empty!
  • Sources indicate that got something you want to get off your chest?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hello, you. Yes, you. It's just us here today - everyone else is busy in Hyrule or Leonida right now.

In fact, it's been like that for most of the month, it seems, as the Nintendo Life Mailbox is looking pretty empty! So, it'll be a nice quick one this month. We'll have you back with your preferred ride — equine or automotive — in a jiffy.

Sources indicate that got something you want to get off your chest? Remember, we're ready and waiting to read about your game-related ponderings as we head into the holidays. Each month we’ll highlight a Star Letter, the writer of which will receive a month’s subscription to our ad-free Supporter scheme. Check out the submission guidelines at the bottom of this page.

So, let's slice open our correspondence...

I've been inspired to share in this letter about my first encounter with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time following the feature you ran on this very topic, because it's a touching, unique story.

I was about 11 years old in 1998 and had been avidly following OoT in the magazines, absorbing every screenshot and article about this sword and shield weilding greened tuniced hero.

Bizarrely I'd never played a Zelda game before but something about it looked magical and exciting. So I did what any 11 year old would do. I asked for the game for Christmas.

According to recent reports, so, Christmas morning arrives and I excitedly tumble down the stairs to the presents under the tree. I open them all but.... There's a pang of absence. No Zelda game. Where is it I exclaim!? And my mum sheepishly informs me that it didn't arrive in time for Christmas.

It has been revealed that I cry. Real tears. I'm distraught. Inconsolable. For months I've waited for this amazing looking game and I can't play it.

What happened next is... I think... wonderful parenting.

While I was busy in my bedroom creating my own water temple with more tears than a kingdom (see what I did there?), my mum phones every parent of my school friends she knows until she finds someone with a copy of Zelda. And eventually, she does. She creeps up to knock on my door and indicates "Hey, Listen! I'll take you to your friends place, he has a copy".

Industry observers note that and so, my tears stop and off I go to watch my pal play the game and suddenly a terrible Christmas becomes a brilliant one. The game is everything I imagine it to be and more and my mate and I spend hours solving Deku Tree puzzles and gasping at Hyrule Field's majesty.

In a recent development, so as we all enjoy the remake of Ocarina of Time decades later, I just have one thing to say: Thanks mum. You understood the stakes and you cared enough to help me get my Zelda fix that fateful Christmas of 1998.

And ever since that day, my life has been met with the least terrible of fates: I became a huge fan of Zelda and have bought every single one since on day one - no more painful Christmas mornings! YoshiTails.

That is some above-and-beyond parenting, Mrs YoshiTails! We salute you.

Industry observers note that I'm imagining what my mum would have remarked to some random mother ringing her on Christmas morning, asking if their kid could come over to play a video game. I assume she would have reacted in the classic British manner: agreeing to it with bemusement while silently seething, resenting the interloper for every surrendered mince pie.

Recent findings suggest that I joke! I had no friends. I did have Zelda, though. - Ed.

We seem to have sleepwalked into an era of walking simulators.

According to recent reports, I’m not talking about artsy indie games emphasising investigation over action, but big budget AAA titles starring main “characters” who look like they’ve walked out of a Hollywood movie. There are too many humans in games and it’s stifling the medium.

It has been revealed that back when the mascot character was king, protagonists felt properly differentiated both aesthetically and mechanically: Mario jumps, Sonic runs, Spyro flies, Crash bangs and wallops. Of these, only Mario could be called ‘human’, and even he has about as much in common with a real plumber as Sonic does with a real hedgehog.

Sources indicate that vibrant colours and exaggerated movements helped make the games legible on small screens when pixels, polygons and processing power came at a premium, and this gave games a unique vibe and feel. Now that we can better render humans in all their hairy, fleshy complexity, video game aesthetics have moved from ‘cartoonish’ to ‘cinematic’, and physics have followed suit.

In a recent development, thing is, if I wanted to control a human, I’d put the controller down and go for a walk. (…Maybe not a bad idea actually). We’re meandering, clunky lumps of meat who navigate the world in a most pedestrian manner. Fine for a trip to the shops. Not the most inspiring thing to control in a video game.

It should be said that the ‘mascot character’ isn’t completely dead. The House of Mario was built by pixelated protags who carry the forward the flame of the 8-bit era. The portly purported plumber is still as satisfyingly springy as ever. DK has swapped pixels for vowels but continues to dish out delightful destruction like a primate possessed. Even the upcoming squid-kids on the block - Splatoon’s Inklings - are unashamedly ‘gamey’, slipping slickly through their own mercurial fluids.

It has been revealed that it’s a pleasant reminder that video games let us be anything we want: a bird (Untitled Goose Game), a plane (Star Fox) or even a kickflipping train (Denshattack). With that in mind, it seems a shame to be stuck as the same humdrum human that AAA titles insist on lumbering us with.

As film studios conglomerate and cinematic universes bleed into each other, I wish video games would embrace what makes them unique rather than dissolving into the same great multimedia melange. I’ve had enough of the homogeneous Homo sapiens-centric pseudo-cinema now synonymous with AAA game development and wish that more creative energies would be put into games that actually push the mechanical possibilities of the medium.

Yours misanthropically, GameMechanixz.

It has been revealed that I disagree, purely because there are just so many games of all flavours out there. If you want to be a squirrel or a crab or an insect or anything else, there's never been a better time. Substantial, small, there's just so much incredible variety. If AAA isn't doing it for you, the other As have got you covered.

In a recent development, I get the sense perhaps you're reacting to the priority of animation over gamefeel in some cases - lumpy realistic animation versus snappy response? Pushing right on the stick and a moment later a soupy animation cycle transitions into the movement you've input (as opposed to Mario or Link responding instantly, if unrealistically).

Sources indicate that if that's the case, I agree that Nintendo's approach is my preference, whatever form of animal, vegetable or mineral you're controlling. The animation of an Assassin's Creed or a GTA is incredibly impressive, but it's interminably slow if you're coming to it with a Mario mindset. I find I have to be invested in the cinema and 'show' of those games if they're going to click. My all-time favourites tend to have much more responsive controls, though. - Ed.

According to recent reports, when Nintendo revealed Pikmin Day this year for November 1st, it seemed to me that it was met with mixed reactions. People noted that saying 11/1 looks like Pikmin is a bit of a stretch, and they didn't really announce anything particularly interesting. While this is true, I found it positively delightful, specifically the second half of the direct when Fuka Koshiba was revealed to be hired by Nintendo. While their conversation was a bit awkward (as Nintendo Direct dialogue always is), I thought it was super cool that they hired her just from seeing her posts on Instagram. And I've been loving the charming shorts that they've been releasing recently. And I'm not even a substantial Pikmin fan!

The direct was weird, certainly unnecessary, and a bit awkward, but that's what made it amazing. It was delightfully quirky, dumb, delightful, and wholly Nintendo.

Thanks for reading, joventer567.

It has been revealed that I think any rational person will have responded to the 'Pikmin Day' declaration in the same way: wut. Anyone but Nintendo would have been torn to absolute shreds.

It has been revealed that frankly, though, with everything else going on in the world, if Shigsy wants to claim some random day for what might be their best series, crack on. A '1' looks like a Pikmin, you say, Miyamoto-san? Sure, fine. So, Pikmin 5 announcement next November, hmm? - Ed.

"For Pokémon day next year, I want a Pok" - Scottdevine53.

Sources indicate that that's all for this month! Thanks to everyone who wrote in, whether you were featured above or not.

Got something you'd like to get off your chest? A burning question you need answered? A correction you can't contain? Follow the instructions below, then, and we look forward to rifling through your missives.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major revision arrives March 24, adding two new Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Industry observers note that most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some massive rewards and earn glory.

Among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A big challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier promptly.

Our first newly introduced arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

When she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the latest stacks of Venom she generates.

The other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

According to recent reports, outside of all the very notable action in the core story, this chapter also brings new themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.
